svg.title: TIDI car wiring — ESP32
svg.text: Drawn as a plan 2026-09-28; the Pi link added 2026-10-19 as Dhairya wired it; the GPS (U8) wired 2026-10-19, not yet read; U4 is now an MG90S. Elsewhere, whether the car matches is unmeasured.
own UPS HAT (E), no car rail
• Every ⏚ is one net: LiPo −, buck IN−/OUT−, ESP32, MDD3A, servos, TF-Luna, Pi.
• Flags with the same name are the same net (+5V, VBAT_SENSE).
• One 5 V rail from the buck. Set it to 5 V and measure before the ESP32 goes on.
GPIO34 is ADC1, so it still reads with WiFi on. Divider is after SW1.
• All ESP32 inputs here are 3.3 V only. Nothing at 5 V may reach a GPIO.
• GPIO32 → M1A, GPIO33 → M1B: the order the firmware should assume.
• GPIO4 is UART2 TX in firmware: leave it unconnected. No strap pins used.
• If the board has no diode between USB and 5V, turn SW1 off before USB goes in.
• No fuse in the LiPo lead yet.
• D1 has no resistor: only GPIO23's driver limits its current. Firmware sets
the pin to its weakest drive. A series resistor is still the safe fix.
• BZ1 is driven straight from GPIO22, as it was on the Arduino. At 3.3 V
instead of 5 V it will be quieter.
• U8 is on the Pi's UART2 (dtoverlay=uart2-pi5). Its VCC is the Pi's 3.3 V,
safe whether or not the GPS board carries its own regulator.
